roslyn-cli — Standalone CLI for Roslyn-powered C# tools

USAGE:
  roslyn-cli <solution-path> <tool-name> [--option value ...]
  roslyn-cli <tool-name> --help
  roslyn-cli --help

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
  --format <json|text>  Output format (default: json)
  --verbose             Show detailed output
  --help, -h            Show this help

DIAGNOSTIC (1):
  diagnose                             Check the health of the Roslyn environment and workspace status

QUERY (12):
  analyze-control-flow                 Analyze control flow paths in a method; startColumn / endColumn (optional) trim the region (1-based; Roslyn Character = column - 1); omitted keeps today's whole-line span (start of startLine through end of endLine); result includes EntryPoints (nodes that transfer control into the region from outside, e.g. goto-targeted labels), ExitPoints, ReturnStatements, and reachability flags
  analyze-data-flow                    Analyze data flow (reads, writes, captures) in a region; startColumn / endColumn (optional) trim the region (1-based; Roslyn Character = column - 1); omitted keeps today's whole-line span (start of startLine through end of endLine)
  find-callers                         Find all callers of a method; callerFile (optional) restricts reported call sites to callers located in that absolute .cs file (applied before maxResults, so totalCount / truncated reflect the filtered set); projectPath (optional) restricts reported call sites to documents in one project of the solution by absolute .csproj path (omit = whole solution), applied before maxResults; namespaceFilter (optional) restricts reported call sites to those whose containing namespace (the code enclosing each call site, not the target symbol) equals it or is nested inside it (ordinal; e.g. App.Services matches App.Services.Orders, not App.ServicesExtra; same matching as search_symbols / find_implementations / find_references namespaceFilter), applied before maxResults; accessibilityFilter (optional: public, internal, protected, private, protected inter
